message:
The top-tier picks from the USC course catalog for your backend engineering goal are CSCI-485 (File and Database Management), which is already in your Fall 2027 plan — great fit there. Right behind it are CSCI-430 (Computer and Network Security), EE-451 (Parallel and Distributed Computation, crosslisted as CSCI-452), and TAC-435 (Professional C++), all scoring 0.9 out of 1.0. These three cover security fundamentals, distributed/cloud computing, and high-performance C++ — all highly relevant for backend work.

CSCI-476 (Cryptography) is a solid 0.7 if you want to go deeper on security, and CSCI-467 (Foundations of Machine Learning) rounds out the mid-tier at 0.5 if you want some ML exposure. All of these have your prerequisites satisfied, so you could slot any of them into your remaining semesters.

You currently have only one technical elective placed (CSCI-485 in Fall 2027), so there's room to add more. If you'd like me to add any of these — say CSCI-430 or EE-451 — to Spring 2027 or Fall 2027, just let me know and I'll propose the change.
